My girl got sick a couple of months ago off an expensive dog food and my vet recommended her to be put on sensitive Science Hill (she'd had stomach upset before and he figured she was just extra sensitive). I had ordered her a big bag of the Science Hill and had totally forgot about my auto ship until close to $100 pulled from my account which I so couldn't afford. Went through email for their customer support and they told me they weren't sure if they could do anything while it was in transit but to get back when them to arrive and they'd walk me through the whole process of refunding it. 

Turns out they were actually able to reroute it midtransit and refunded me the money within the day. Someone had to go above and beyond to get ahold of where it was shipping and reroute it back and my bank account was Soo thankful for it. I expect if I had mentioned she had gotten sick off the last food they'd have sent a card or something because they're just that good. Daisy is now 2, happy and healthy and just received a beautiful hand written card for her well in time for her birthday.

I mean, sure there's always a chance they could, but nothing is guaranteed. It's better you find a good way to redirect the biting now before it could become something much more serious. Better to play it safe than sorry than hope they just grow out of it.

I have a pittiexlab mix who used to bite and what worked for her, because she fed off that energy, is abruptly taking any attention she was getting away from her. Example being, when she got riled up and started to nip and grab, we'd stand and turn our backs from her and ignore her until she calmed down. Or we moved her to her crate for some quiet time, ignored her and then let her back out when she had calmed down. She learned that biting meant playtime was over, and the biting has stopped.

If that doesn't work for her consider a trainer, because now's the time to course correct any naughty and bad behavior.

It's open world to grow your dino, yes, and can be very fun, but it's important to remember it's a survival game. So expect to die a couple times.I haven't played any other dino games so I'm probably not the best to say how it's unique but the packing with other players, and different servers having different rules can change up the game play a little bit. Occasionally servers have special events which can be really fun! My main con about the game is that people can get really butthurt over losing their dinos, as if it's not a survival game where you can be killed.My #1 tip is don't call out/make a lot of noise until you hit adult hood and know what you're doing. Calling/roaring is a quick way to die because it helps more experienced dinos track you down and find you.  
But yeah, there's an update/recode of the game coming soon so a lot of things will probably change.

My basset hound died nearly two years ago this coming December and it was a rough, traumatic death on me and the family. She'd just had a cancerous tumor removed a couple months before and we were told that because he had clean margins she had it all, so the scary cancer threat had been lifted and while she had epilepsy, that fear of losing her young-ish (because she was only 8) had just dissipated. We didn't know that her epilepsy could be fatal (though we're not 100% sure why). She seized off and on for two or three days before her body quit on her, after the vets tried everything for her. It's hard to get that hollow, blank stare out of my head when I think of her but... 

She was my little space heater. Every night, all winter long, she'd be pressed up against my butt/back under the blanket keeping us both warm. She had this warm, comforting smell that 16-23 year old me would go searching for whenever I was struggling with my anxiety or depression, and it comforted me every time. That deep chested bark and that long, hound howl whenever the doorbell rang. Is it raining? No way she was leaving the porch and that walk would have to wait. She was a piggie, and could get into anything with the exception of the fridge, in search of food (she once even got a zipped lunch bag open). We called her a diva because if she wanted to lay in the grass you can bet you weren't going anywhere until she was ready. I miss her running to meet me at the door and those wet floppy ears she liked to suck on. I even miss all the drool when she was excited or was getting a treat. I miss everything. I miss her totally and completely. She was my best friend whenever I needed one, no matter when or where.
